In Class 9, I had a skin rash on my arms that wouldn't go away for months. I pulled my sleeves down over my hands every day, even in the heat. I hunched my shoulders, trying to hide.
I thought everyone was staring.
One day in art class, Preeti sat next to me. She didn't ask about my sleeves. She just talked about her drawing and asked me to help with the colours.
She treated me like normal. After a few weeks, I stopped pulling my sleeves so much.
Later she told me she'd noticed, but she didn't want to make me feel worse.
- Samir

qa.a: The sleeves.

qa.q: What was Samir feeling while hiding the arms?
qa.a: Samir felt embarrassed and self-conscious, worried everyone was staring at the rash.

qa.q: What did Preeti do that helped?
qa.a: She treated Samir normally, didn't mention the sleeves, and offered steady acceptance through friendship.

qa.q: How might Preeti have felt seeing Samir hide?
qa.a: Preeti probably felt caring and wanted to help without making Samir feel worse.

grounding: The narrator recalls hiding a rash with sleeves and hunching, and a friend's steady acceptance helping.

Class teacher's note, Wednesday
I've noticed Lalit hunches, pulls up his hood and covers his face with his hands every time a particular senior from the school bus walks past. He doesn't do this with anyone else.
Today I asked him to stay after class. I told him I'd noticed he seemed uneasy around that student, and asked if something was going on.
At first he just shrugged. Then he said the senior takes his lunch money and threatens him on the bus.
I told him it wasn't his fault and thanked him for telling me. This afternoon I informed the school's safeguarding lead and called his parents. Lalit will sit near the bus monitor from tomorrow.
- Ms Sarita

qa.q: Where does Lalit sit from tomorrow?
qa.a: Near the bus monitor.

qa.q: What was Lalit feeling when he hunched and covered his face?
qa.a: Lalit felt afraid and uneasy, trying to avoid notice by the senior who threatened him.

qa.q: What did Ms Sarita do that protected Lalit?
qa.a: She noticed the pattern, asked gently, told him it wasn't his fault, informed the safeguarding lead and his parents that afternoon, and moved his seat.

qa.q: How might Lalit's parents feel when Ms Sarita called?
qa.a: They would likely feel worried but grateful the teacher noticed and acted quickly.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a teenager shielding his face around one person as fear, and a trusted adult acting the same day.

Thursday
The barber cut my hair way too short today. I looked in the mirror and wanted to cry. I pulled my hood up and kept my head down all the way home.
Nazia saw me at the gate. I covered my face with my hands. "Don't look."
She laughed a little, then said, "Abhinav, it's just hair. You're still you."
She didn't make fun. She just walked with me to the shop and bought us both samosas.
By the end, I took my hood off. I still feel weird, but less.
- Abhinav
